corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN, with more of it known than the checker said. Given the chain lemma (H upper triangular with unit diagonal, so |det H|=1), the inequality part of Lemma cost for all 0<r<=1, Prop. gen and Remark 'other penalties' all follow from Rotfel'd's trace inequality (Thompson 1976, Thm 3(i)/eq. (1)) plus Jensen/AM-GM on log singular values. This covers every concave increasing psi with psi(0)=0 and psi∘exp convex, a strictly larger class than TBF. Genuinely ours: the chain lemma, and the equality case (exactly nu neurons, equal moduli, orthogonal chain vectors). Prop. esym is a textbook Cauchy-Binet/Hadamard intermediate and is not needed for the inequality.
issues: Both confirmed citations check out. Rajan-Tepedelenlioglu arXiv 1302.5383: PDF text read. Def. 1, eq. (6) TBF, Property S1 and App. A eqs. (28)-(31) are as the checker described. Crossref confirms TIT 61(4):1619-1628. Schilling-Song-Vondracek: ETH TOC shows Ch. 8 'Thorin-Bernstein functions' starting p. 73. Crossref confirms de Gruyter, issued 2009-12-24, print year 2010. Missed prior art: Rotfel'd's trace inequality as proved by Thompson (Pacific J. Math 66(1):285-290, 1976), which holds for arbitrary square matrices: sum f(sigma(A+B)) <= sum f(sigma(A)) + sum f(sigma(B)) for f concave, increasing, f(0)=0. Applied to H = sum_l d_l u_l u_l^* (rank-one singular values |d_l|), it gives sum psi(|d_l|) >= sum psi(sigma_i(H)). Since |det H|=1 by the chain lemma, Jensen on log sigma_i gives >= nu psi(1) whenever psi∘exp is convex, which every TBF satisfies. Numerically sanity-checked on 20k random instances. So the checker's recommended wording, which calls the domination (Lemma chain + Prop. esym) the new ingredient, overclaims. The domination is a corollary of the chain lemma plus a 1969/1976 matrix inequality. The paper's determinant/Bernstein route is still needed for the equality case, which the Rotfel'd route does not give. Recommend citing Thompson 1976 (Rotfel'd) in Remark 'other penalties' and presenting the generating-function proof as a self-contained route that also yields equality.
